Subject: Initial redlines — privacy addendum and subprocessors

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send over FinHealth's redlines to the privacy addendum so we can get DocuSign queued. Attached is our annotated PDF (FinHealth_DPA_redlines_v3.pdf) and a current subprocessors inventory. Key asks:

- Confirmation of EU->US transfer mechanism (we requested SCCs + describe transfer flows)
- Subprocessor list with last-modified date and an assurance cadence
- KMS/customer-managed keys: procurement flagged this as a hard requirement for PHI-adjacent workloads
- Standard liability cap language in section 9 (we proposed a carve-out for security incidents)

We are aiming to have legal sign-off and DocuSign executed by Apr 5 to align with our go-live. Can Redwood confirm whether the KMS requirement is negotiable or if an exception workflow is available?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Morales
Head of Procurement, FinHealth

Hi Aisha — thanks for the redlines and the subprocessors CSV. We received the attachments and started an internal review. Quick notes:

- We can provide SCCs and a current subprocessors roster (will confirm dates).
- KMS (customer-managed keys) is non-standard for hosted Redwood; that will need a formal exception and Security sign-off. I'm looping in Rishi from Legal and Monica from Customer Success so they have context.
- DocuSign: we can prepare an execution packet, but we will need to resolve the KMS and a couple of liability redlines before we can finalize.

Proposed next steps:
1) Legal to send consolidated comments by end of day Tue 3/30
2) We escalate KMS request to Risk/InfoSec for exception consideration (target response by Fri 4/2)
3) If approved, we will push DocuSign and aim for execution next week

If your deadline of Apr 5 is firm, please confirm — we'll prioritize accordingly but need clarity on the timeline.

Cheers,
Priyom Das

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: pri_yom_das@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Initial redlines — privacy addendum and subprocessors

Team — ran a pass on the client's PDF and compiled high-level redline notes (attached: legal_comments_dpa.txt). Summary:

- SCCs: ok to accept; need to confirm which transfer mechanisms apply to specific data types.
- Subprocessors: provide last-12-month change log and a roll-forward process; offer quarterly notice.
- Liability: their proposed carve-out is broader than we can accept; propose capped indemnity tied to direct damages.
- KMS: material security change. Customer-managed keys is not part of our hosted offering; approving an exception creates operational and compliance risk (key escrow, rotation, recovery). This is an Exception Request that needs Security (Vivek/TBD) and Legal leadership sign-off.

Risk level: HIGH for KMS. If Procurement's go-live date is immovable, we should evaluate temporary mitigations (e.g., Dedicated instance + contractual controls + timeline for KMS roadmap) and include a remediation plan in the contract.

I'll prepare redline language for the liability and subprocessors sections and can join a call with FinHealth if helpful.

-Rishi
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Morales <aisha.morales@finhealth.io>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — privacy addendum and subprocessors

Hi Aisha — appreciate the quick turnaround. I wanted to be transparent on where we are on each ask: 

- SCCs/Subprocessors: We will provide the full subprocessors inventory and a link to the SCCs PDF by EOD Wed 3/31.
- Liability: Legal proposes alternative wording; Rishi attached suggested language.
- KMS: This is the blocker. Legal categorizes it as a high-risk exception. We can pursue two paths:
  1) Exception: Submit to Risk Committee for review this week — if approved, include an implementation timeline and operational controls in the exhibit.
  2) Short-term mitigation: Offer Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity + private VPC) with contractual commitments on key access controls as an interim step while we roadmap KMS support.

If you can give us until Mon 4/12 to fully resolve KMS (exception + remediation plan), we will commit to prioritized handling. If Apr 5 is a hard deadline, we need to understand if FinHealth will accept the mitigation path so we can prepare DocuSign accordingly.

--
Priyom Das
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Morales <aisha.morales@finhealth.io>

Cc: Mark Benton <mbenton@finhealth.io>, procurement@finhealth.io
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 07:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines — privacy addendum and subprocessors

Priyom — thanks for the update. Unfortunately Apr 5 is firm for our procurement timetable (board approval window). We cannot move the go-live schedule without material cost. A few clarifications and asks: 

- We will accept SCCs and the subprocessors list, but the KMS requirement is non-negotiable for our PHI-adjacent workload. If Redwood cannot support customer-managed keys in hosted in time, we need a written exception that includes:
  * explicit timeline to deliver KMS or equivalent controls
  * signed attestation of key handling practices in the interim

- Alternative (acceptable to us): If Redwood can commit to a Dedicated deployment with contractual controls (private VPC, dedicated tenancy, documented access controls) and execute DocuSign by Apr 5, FinHealth can proceed.

I have looped in our CFO Mark Benton to underscore the timeline. Can Redwood escalate to legal leadership immediately? We need a yes/no before end of day Mon 4/5 or FinHealth will need to pull the current release window.

Regards,
Aisha
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Aisha — understood and thanks for the clarity. I'm escalating to our Risk Committee and Legal leadership with your asks and the proposed time constraint. Attached is an escalation note for the committee (escalation_note_for_risk_committee.pdf).

Proposed immediate path:
- We will prioritize a dedicated risk review this afternoon and aim to provide a decision on exception vs Dedicated mitigation by EOD Mon 4/5.
- If the committee grants an exception, we will include a contractual remediation schedule and an attestation covering interim key handling.
- If exception is not feasible, we'll fast-track a Dedicated offering contract packet for DocuSign with the security exhibits required by FinHealth.

I'll follow up as soon as I have formal guidance. Thanks for flagging the board deadline — that helps prioritize.

Best,
Priyom
